url_citation.title: Bob Kierlin – Public Profile
url_citation.content:
Bob Kierlin
Birthplace
Winona, Minnesota
Bob attended Cotter High School and later earned a Bachelor of Mechanical Engineering and a Master’s in Business Management at the University of Minnesota.
After two years as a Peace Corps volunteer in Venezuela, he joined IBM as a cost engineer and financial planner. At age 12, Bob envisioned a business plan to sell threaded fasteners through vending machines and, with four friends, founded Fastenal in 1967.
Fastenal evolved from a small-town shop into a multibillion-dollar global company. Bob was the company’s CEO until 2002 and President until 2001. Additionally, he served as a Minnesota State Senator from 1999 to 2006 and retired from Fastenal’s board in 2014, continuing as a mentor and advisor.
Known for his frugal lifestyle, Bob drives company vehicles and ties his net worth to Fastenal stock rather than bonuses. In 1997, he authored “The Power of Fastenal People,” sharing his leadership principles and emphasizing the importance of empowering others.
Bob is active in various community and educational boards, notably the Hiawatha Education Foundation, which supports Minnesota’s preschool Montessori programs, and he participates in local development projects in Winona, Minnesota.
